summary: Saa'ib bin Yazeed, as a boy, went out with the people of Madinah to Thaniyyatul Wadaa to welcome the Prophet back from Tabook.
notes: Saa'ib bin Yazeed may be the approved saaib (Saa'ib); left unlinked because the vocab entry has no patronymic.

summary: Umar says the Prophet marched to Badr and to the conquest of Makkah during Ramadhaan.

Umar and Ibn Abbaas report the numbers at Badr, that the Sahabah did not fast on those two Ramadhaan campaigns, and that the Prophet left Madinah on the tenth of Ramadhaan with Abu Ruhm Kulthoom as deputy.
notes: Several separate reports from different narrators are joined in one entry (the Badr numbers, the departure, the fast at Kudayd).

summary: On the march to Makkah during Ramadhaan the Prophet drank water in full view at midday so that the thirsty Sahabah would follow him in breaking their fast.

Ibn Abbaas reports the Prophet's ruling that a non-Mahram man and woman must not be alone together and a woman must not travel without a Mahram, and that he told a Sahabi whose wife had gone for Hajj to perform Hajj with her instead of joining an expedition.
notes: The Sahabi who asked is unnamed and so is not tagged.

summary: Ka'b reports that on returning from a journey in the morning the Prophet would first enter the Masjid and pray two rak'ahs.
notes: Ka'b alone is ambiguous (Ka'b bin Maalik, Ka'b bin Zuhayr and others share the name); left unlinked.

summary: Jaabir reports that when he returned with the Prophet from a journey, the Prophet told him to enter the Masjid and pray two rak'ahs.
notes: Linked to jaabir-bin-abdillaah by the usual reading of Jaabir alone; the text gives no patronymic.

summary: Jaabir reports that the Prophet had a cow slaughtered for the Sahabah on the way back, and on reaching Madinah sent him to pray two rak'ahs before paying him the price of his camel.
notes: Two wordings of the same Jaabir report are joined in one entry. Linked as in n00767.

summary: Aa'isha recounts how she was left behind on the Banu Mustaliq expedition, was brought back by Safwaan bin Mu'attal, and how slander spread through the army and Madinah, with the Prophet hearing of it and consulting Ali, Usaama and Bareerah.
notes: The Quranic quotation and the final lines are badly garbled by OCR (e.g. the Surah Yusuf passage) and the text breaks off mid-sentence; the story is completed in n00770 and n00771. Zaynab bint Jahash is left unlinked because the vocab zaynab has no patronymic. Usayd and Sa'd bin Ubaadah are placed by the text's own description.

summary: Aa'isha describes the revelation that confirmed her innocence, the Prophet wiping sweat from his face and giving her the good news, and his order that Mistah, Hassaan and Hamna be given the prescribed punishment.
notes: Opening lines are heavily garbled by OCR and the entry starts mid-story. Still readable as narration of the same event.

summary: Aa'isha reports that she refused her mother's urging to thank the Prophet, that Abu Bakr stopped supporting Mistah until the verse of forgiveness was revealed, and that he then resumed his support.
notes: Opens as a new narration in a detailed version of the same event. The Quran quotations are OCR-garbled. Aa'isha's mother is not named and so is not tagged.

summary: A woman of Banu Ghifaar went out with the Prophet to Khaybar to nurse the wounded; after she first menstruated he told her how to clean the saddle, and after the victory he gave her a necklace that she kept until her death.
notes: The woman narrator is unnamed, so she is not given a person entry.

summary: Humayd bin Hilaal reports that the Prophet described a woman who lost a goat and her needle on a journey, prayed to Allaah, and had both restored by the next morning.
notes: The man from Banu Tufaawa who passed on the report is unnamed. The Prophet tells the story as an example, so he is marked subject.

summary: Anas reports that the Prophet dreamt of his Ummah sailing the sea in the path of Allaah, and that Ummu Haraam was promised a place in the first group; she later went on a naval expedition and died after a fall from her animal.
notes: Mu'aawiya appears as Hadhrat Mu'aawiya with no patronymic; the vocab entry muaawiya is marked unsure. Only the Mu'aawiya link is uncertain.

summary: Ummu Sulaym reports that women of the Ansaar marched with the Prophet on expeditions to give water to the sick and treat the wounded.
Anas reports that Ummu Sulaym and other women of the Ansaar marched with the Prophet on expeditions to provide water and tend the wounded.
notes: The final characters are OCR debris and are ignored.

summary: Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh reports that when women were with the Prophet on expeditions they gave water to the soldiers, treated the wounded and brought back the dead.
Rubayyi bint Mu'awwidh, quoted by Bukhari, describes women fetching water and bringing back the dead and wounded, and Ummu Atiyya says she went on seven expeditions cooking and nursing.
notes: Two reports (Rubayyi quoted by Bukhari, and Ummu Atiyya's own account) are joined in one entry.

summary: Layla Ghifaariyya reports that she went on expeditions with the Prophet to nurse the wounded.
Anas saw Aa'isha and Ummu Sulaym carrying water to the wounded at Uhud; Tha'laba reports that Umar gave a cloth to Ummu Saleet, who had sewn water-skins at Uhud, rather than to Ummu Kulthoom.
notes: Two separate reports (Anas at Uhud; Tha'laba and Umar's cloth) are joined in one entry. Ummu Saleet is not in the vocab and is given no patronymic in the text.

summary: A grandmother of Hashraj bin Ziyaad reports that women went with the Prophet to Khaybar to weave ropes, nurse the wounded and give barley porridge, and Zuhri adds that women gave water to the fighters.
notes: Two reports (the grandmother's and Zuhri's) are joined in one entry. The grandmother herself is unnamed.

summary: Ummu Sa'd reports from Ummu Ammaara that at Uhud, when the Muslims were losing, she fought close to the Prophet, took many wounds, and struck Ibn Qami'a, who had wounded her, with her sword.
notes: The text spells the attacker 'Ibn Qami'Ahmad' (OCR); read as Ibn Qami'a. Mus'ab bin Umayr is linked as named in the text.

summary: Umaarah bint Ghaziyyah reports that at Uhud Ummu Ammaara killed a Mushrik horseman; Umar reports the Prophet saying he saw her fighting in his defence on every side, and Umar sends her a valuable shawl over Safiyya bint Ubayd.
notes: Three reports from different narrators (Umaarah; Umar; Hamza bin Sa'eed) are joined in one entry.

summary: Hishaam, reporting from his father, says that when the Muslims were losing at Uhud Safiyya came with a spear to drive them back, and the Prophet told Zubayr to look after his mother.
Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib reports that during the Battle of the Trench she killed a Jewish man who was circling the fort where the women and children were, because Hassaan would not do it.
notes: The Jewish man is unnamed and so is not tagged.

summary: Anas reports that at Hunayn Ummu Sulaym kept a dagger ready to stab any Mushrik who came near her, and the Prophet asked her about it and smiled, while Abu Talha laughed about it.
Muhaajir reports that Asmaa bint Yazeed killed nine Romans with a tent peg at the Battle of Yarmook.
notes: The narrator's name is only 'Muhaajir'; the vocab entries for that name are different people, so left unlinked.

summary: Ummu Kabsha asked the Prophet for permission to join an expedition to nurse the wounded and give water; he refused, saying he feared it would become a regular practice, and told her to stay at home.
Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports a woman's question to the Prophet about women's reward compared with men's jihaad, and his answer that obedience to a husband and fulfilling his rights equals it.
notes: Two versions (the Ibn Abbaas report and the Tabraani version) are joined in one entry. The woman is unnamed.

summary: Sha'bi reports that a woman gave her young son a sword to fight at Uhud, the Prophet directed the boy's attacks, and when the boy was wounded the Prophet asked if he was frightened.
notes: The mother and the boy are unnamed and not tagged.

summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that the Prophet sent his brother Umayr back from Badr as too young, that Umayr wept until he was allowed to go, and that Sa'd tied knots in Umayr's sword belt to fit him.
Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that his brother Umayr hid to avoid being sent back from Badr, was allowed to go after weeping, and was martyred at sixteen.
Ibn Is'haaq reports Abu Bakr's sermon at the orchard of the Banu Saa'idah that two leaders for the Muslims leads to dissension, the abandonment of the Sunnah and the rise of bid'ah.
notes: The sermon is cited via Ibn Is'haaq with no chain. The entry ends with an OCR artefact.

summary: Umar says two swords cannot share one sheath, and Abu Dharr, after criticising Uthmaan's four rak'ahs, quotes the Prophet's warning against disgracing rulers and the three duties owed to them.
notes: Heavily garbled by OCR; the Umar and Abu Dharr passages are joined and part of the salaah report is missing, so who said what is uncertain. The unnamed Ansaar speaker is not tagged.

summary: Qataada reports that Uthmaan prayed four rak'ahs at Mina in the later years of his caliphate, and that Ibn Mas'ood, after reciting Innaa lillaahi, prayed four behind him too, saying opposing the leader causes more harm.
notes: OCR garbles part of the Quran phrase and the start of the chain. The Prophet is mentioned only as the one whose practice is described.

summary: Ali says he dislikes disunity and advises people to keep the practice of the earlier caliphs; he tells Ibnul Kawwaa that the Sunnah is the Prophet's way and unity is the consensus of the truth, and Ibn Seereen says narrations from extreme groups attributed to Ali are false.
notes: The text ends at a section heading ('The Standpoint of the Sahabah concerning the Khilaafah') that belongs to the next section of the book.

summary: Urwa bin Zubayr reports that Abu Bakr came after the Prophet's death, uncovered his face, kissed him, rejected Umar's claim that he had not died, and gave a sermon quoting the verse that Muhammad is only a Messenger.
notes: Umar is referred to as 'the son of Khattaab' in Abu Bakr's words; linked to umar on that basis.

summary: Umar exclaims that he had forgotten the Quranic verse about the Prophet's death, and Abu Bakr recites verses stating that all will die and only Allaah remains.
notes: Continues the sermon begun in n00797. Quranic quotations are OCR-garbled in places.

summary: Abu Bakr tells the people that the Prophet completed his mission, that whoever worshipped Allaah should know Allaah lives, that whoever worshipped Muhammad should know he has died, and that the Qur'aan is a light and a cure.
notes: Continues the sermon begun in n00798. Ends with the Muhaajireen going with Abu Bakr to the burial, and an OCR marker '(I)'.

summary: Anas reports Umar's sermon the day after the Prophet's death urging the people to pledge to Abu Bakr, and Abu Ubaydah saying he will not step ahead of the one the Prophet made imam of salaah; a second statement by Abu Ubaydah calls Abu Bakr the second of the two in the cave.
notes: Several reports from different narrators (Anas; Zuhri; Abul Bakhtari; Abu Ubaydah's statements) are joined in one entry. Abu Ubaydah's second statement is the same person as the one in the first part of this entry.
